messages:
Maya (People Ops): Quick ask  we're getting multiple requests for an expedited sign-off flow because of an external vendor audit next week. Instead of 'backup', can teams nominate a deputy reviewer who has delegated authority to triage and append final notes if the primary can't sign by the cutoff? Please post deputy name + Lattice handle + delegation scope by NOON tomorrow.
Lewis (ENG Manager): Deputy flow sounds good. Quick clarification: can a deputy change a rating if they're stepping in, or only annotate and hand back to the manager for final approval?
Maya (People Ops): Deputies can be given limited delegation. Default: deputies annotate and finalize only in these cases: PTO verified, travel with no Lattice access, or incident involvement >2hrs. If manager wants full delegation, add comment `delegated-final: <deputy name> (reason)` in the review before EOD. We'll capture that in the audit packet.
Asha (Security): If the review contains any security-restricted evidence, tag the review `sec-only`. Deputies without clearance must be given a redacted evidence set and add `redacted: true` in their reviewer note.
Nora (Product): How do we capture delegation in an auditable way? We need an easy CSV export for the vendor audit.
Maya (People Ops): Use this deputy template (paste verbatim into the review comment):
```
Deputy: Name (Lattice handle)
Scope: annotate-only | finalize-if-absent | full-delegation
Reason: PTO / travel / incident / other
Delegation-notes: <short text>
```
We'll pull all comments that match `Deputy:` for the audit CSV.
Hiro (SRE): One of our reviewers will be on-call during the audit window. If we mark them as `on-call` in the comment, does that auto-trigger the deputy?
Maya (People Ops): Not automatically. Mark `on-call: incident-<id>` and assign a deputy. We'll treat that as a valid reason for deputy finalization. Also note: if incident >2hrs, reviewer gets a 24-hour extension by policy, but auditing deadlines may still require finalization via deputy.
Lewis (ENG Manager): Can we get a short, single-sentence script for deputies to use so language in calibration doesn't diverge? Last cycle the writeups varied and made calibration noisy.
Maya (People Ops): Yes. Deputies should use this shorthand at the top of their note: `Deputy-note: reviewed against rubric; 1 strength; 1 growth; final rating (if delegated): X; rationale: <1-2 sentences>`. If not delegated, use `Deputy-note: annotated-only; observations: <1-2 lines>`.
Asha (Security): Also reminder: remove any PII from evidence before deputies in different jurisdictions see it. Use `redact-checklist.md` from the shared folder.
Nora (Product): If the deputy changes the rating by >1 band, do we need to flag a calibration exception?
Maya (People Ops): Yes. Any change >1 band triggers a calibration exception. Deputies should add `cal-exception: true` with a 1-line justification so we can queue it for rapid review.
people-ops-bot: Reminder scheduled: "Submit deputy nominations" in 8 hours. :bell:
Hiro (SRE): Noted. I'll nominate Aya (Lattice: @aya-sre) as deputy with `finalize-if-absent` and tag the on-call incident when it starts.
Lewis (ENG Manager): Added deputy: Samira (@samira-eng) scope `annotate-only` for Team Atlas. Posting the comment now.
Maya (People Ops): Thanks all. If you need temporary permissions for deputies to view evidence, DM me `grant-temp <Lattice-handle>` and include the review id. We'll try to keep the audit CSV clean. If anything changes after the bot reminder, DM and cc people-ops@redwood.com.
